title: Jaeger HTTP collector compatibility adapter for legacy SDKs with envelope batching and tenant mapping
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Several Redwood customers still send spans using legacy Jaeger HTTP Thrift/JSON collectors and older SDKs that do not support OTLP. Our current ingest path expects OTLP/gRPC or OTLP/HTTP and drops or misattributes these legacy envelopes. This ticket implements a compatibility adapter that accepts Jaeger HTTP payloads, translates them to our internal OTLP-like span model, attaches tenant metadata (from API keys or tenant headers), and forwards them into the existing trace pipeline (Tempo backend).

Goals:
- Accept Jaeger agent/collector HTTP endpoints (both thrift and jaeger-json) at a dedicated compatibility endpoint behind the trace gateway.
- Batch and envelope spans in a way that is friendly to Tempo (preserve trace IDs, span IDs, tags).
- Map legacy client tenant identifiers to our tenant namespace (fall back to API-key routing).
- Emit transformation telemetry so we can monitor loss, drop rate, and latency added by the adapter.

Non-goal: This adapter is not a full feature parity shim for every custom tag — we will map core attributes and surface unmapped tags as raw_metadata for downstream analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility endpoint accepts Jaeger thrift POSTs and returns 202 on success
Spans are visible in Tempo-backed trace UI with preserved trace/span IDs
Tenant mapping works for API-key header and jaeger.tags.client_id -> tenant mapping table
Adapter adds <10ms median processing latency at p50 with 1k rps synthetic load (measured in canary)
Transformation telemetry (processed, dropped, parse_errors) is exported to observability dashboards
technical_notes:
Architecture: Add a light-weight 'jaeger-compat' route to the trace gateway service that performs: parse -> validate -> map-tenant -> normalize -> envelope to internal span format -> forward to trace-ingest worker pool. Use existing worker pool and backpressure queues.

Parsing: Use thrift parser for binary payloads and a forgiving json parser for legacy jaeger-json variations. Fallback parsing attempts should be rate-limited and counted in telemetry.

Batching: Group incoming spans by tenant and trace_id up to 50 spans or 50ms, whichever comes first, then forward as a single internal envelope to keep Tempo ingest efficiency.

Tenant mapping: Primary: look up tenant via Authorization header (Bearer <ingest-key>). Secondary: read jaeger.tags.client_id and consult tenant-mapping redis cache with TTL; if not found, tag as 'unmapped' and send to quarantine topic for later reconciliation.

Backpressure and safety: Reuse existing ingest backpressure signals: if downstream buffer > 80% mark, reply 429 to producers (best-effort) and enqueue diagnostic event. Avoid blocking main gateway threads.

Telemetry: Emit metrics: jaeger_compat.received, .parsed, .dropped, .forwarded, .parse_latency_ms histogram, and a sample of transformed span payloads to an internal bucket for debugging behind RBAC.

Security: Validate request size and throttle per-IP to avoid amplification. Reject unauthenticated requests immediately.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy adapter in internal alpha mode behind feature flag and only allow list of 3 pilot tenants. 2) Run synthetic load tests and validate Tempo visibility and latency. 3) Open canary to 10% of edge nodes and monitor transformation metrics & error budgets for 48h. 4) Gradually expand tenant allowlist over 2 weeks, then enable global acceptance. 5) Flip feature flag off if >1% parse_error or >0.5% dropped spans from adapter for 30m.
qa_steps: Run unit tests for thrift/json parsers with saved legacy payloads
End-to-end test: Send sample jaeger-thrift POST to canary adapter, verify spans in Tempo UI with expected service.name and tags
Load test: 1k rps synthetic jaeger clients, verify p50/p95 adapter processing latency and 429 behavior under load
Security test: attempt oversized payload, ensure 413 response and no memory leak
Failure test: simulate downstream queue full, verify upstream 429 and adapter logs a backpressure event
risks:
- Parser edge cases may silently drop uncommon thrift fields (we will log raw payload samples).
- Tenant mapping misses could cause spans to be quarantined and not visible to customers.
- Added processing layer increases ingest latency; must be tightly monitored.
- Rate-limiting behavior varies across legacy clients and may increase customer confusion.
